description: Minecraft Fabric mod adding legendary items and loot

mods.name: Legendaries
mods.description: Unique, one-per-world legendary items with their own crafting recipes and rules.

releases.notes:
**The legendaries have names now.** A netherite pickaxe that is *the* Legendary Pickaxe no longer
sits in your inventory looking exactly like the one you made this morning: five of the six carry a
name of their own — the **Legendary Spear**, **Legendary Mace**, **Legendary Pickaxe**, **Legendary
Sword** and **Legendary Axe** — written in a gradient of the same molten amber the textures set into
the metal, deep at the first letter and bright at the last.

**The Dragon Egg keeps the vanilla name.** It is the one legendary you can never mistake for
something else, because there has only ever been one dragon egg.

**The name needs no resource pack.** It is an ordinary vanilla component, so it reaches every client
with nothing installed — unlike the textures, which are still an optional pack.

**A legendary you crafted before this has no name.** An item's components are fixed when it is made
and the name is written by the recipe, so it rides on the ones made from here on; putting an old one
on the pedestal and taking it back does not add one either.

**The world hears when one arrives.** The first time a legendary is in anybody's hands, the server
announces it to everyone:

```
The Legendary Pickaxe has been crafted by Steve
The Dragon Egg has been obtained by Alex
```

Once per world, not once per player — it marks the legendary arriving, not somebody acquiring it, so
handing it over, dying with it and claiming it back off the pedestal are all silent. A legendary your
world already had is announced the first time somebody picks it up after updating, since nothing
recorded the arrival at the time.

**The Netherite Spear is now the Legendary Spear, and the Mace the Legendary Mace**, in the mod's
messages as well as on the item. Nothing about either changed — the spear is still the only spear
you can get, still crafted from the same nine things, and the mace recipe is still vanilla's.

**Molten Blast's countdown** is written in the deep end of that same amber, where it was a lighter
orange of its own.

**Trying to put the Dragon Egg down** now says `The Dragon Egg cannot be placed.` rather than the
longer "will not be set down as a block".

**For operators — the command names changed, and the old ones stop working.** Every legendary now
answers to the name the item itself carries: `netherite_spear` → `legendary_spear`, `mace` →
`legendary_mace`, `pickaxe` → `legendary_pickaxe`, `sword` → `legendary_sword`, `axe` →
`legendary_axe`. Only `dragon_egg` is unchanged. That is what `item give`, `item delete` and
`config` take and tab-complete; a command block or macro still running an old name fails with
"unknown legendary", so retype those before you update.

Still one jar for Minecraft 26.1 through the 26.3 line, and still nothing for other players to
install.

releases.notes:
**Fix: a single-player world would not finish loading.**

Since 0.6.0, opening your own world offered you the resource pack the way a server does — and taking
it left the world stuck on "Loading Terrain". Nothing had crashed; the resource reload the pack
triggers was landing in the middle of the join, and the join never completed.

Only a dedicated server offers the pack now. That is the surface Minecraft itself implements — a
single-player world has never pushed a resource pack, and it turns out there is a reason.

**Single-player installs the pack by hand instead.** The zip is attached to the release on GitHub,
next to the jar. Drop it in `.minecraft/resourcepacks` and turn it on once in Options → Resource
Packs. That is better than the offer was even when the offer worked: the selection sticks between
sessions, where the prompt asked again every single time you opened the world — single-player has no
server entry, and that is the only place a "yes, always" answer could be kept.

**A world opened to LAN counts as single-player here**, so guests are not offered the pack either.
Nothing was broken for them, but the mod is asked this question once per server rather than once per
player. Pass them the zip along with the invite.

Nothing changes on a dedicated server: it offers the pack on join exactly as before, still optional,
still declinable, and an operator's own `resource-pack` line still wins.

No gameplay changes. Every legendary, recipe and rule is exactly as it was in 0.7.0.

mods.description: Unique, one-per-world legendary items with their own crafting recipes and rules.

releases.notes:
Two more legendaries, and the first two that are weapons you already know how to make: the
**Legendary Sword** and the **Legendary Axe**.

**Ordinary swords and axes are untouched.** Each of these has a recipe of its own rather than
replacing vanilla's, so everything you could make before you can still make.

**One recipe shape, two items** — the far ends of the game, around the tool you are upgrading:

|   |   |   |
|---|---|---|
| Dragon breath | Dragon head | Dragon breath |
| Echo shard | *Netherite sword or axe* | Echo shard |
| Nether star | Sharpness V book | Nether star |

Two nether stars apiece means two withers apiece; the dragon head is mined off an End city ship, the
breath is bottled from the dragon mid-fight, and the echo shards come out of ancient city chests.
These cost more than anything else in the mod.

**The book is checked when you take the result**, the way the pickaxe's are — a recipe can ask for
an enchanted book and cannot ask what is written in it, so the wrong enchantment gives you a result
that refuses to come out and says why.

**The Sword** is unbreakable, carries **Sharpness VIII, Fire Aspect III and Looting III**, and gives
**Speed** while it is in your inventory or your hand. Sharpness VIII is three levels past the
vanilla ceiling the Netherite Spear carries, making it the fastest-killing thing here — though the
Axe, which starts two damage higher and takes the same Sharpness bonus, lands the bigger single hit.

**The Axe** is unbreakable, carries **Sharpness VIII, Silk Touch and Efficiency V**, and gives
**Strength**. Silk Touch on an axe is what takes a bee nest with its bees still in it. Efficiency V
rather than the pickaxe's VI, so the pickaxe stays the better tool for what a pickaxe is for.

**Both keep every rule the others do** — one per world, refused by every container, never set down as
a block, returned to the pedestal rather than lost. The pedestal now holds six; a world that already
has one rebuilds its plinth on the next load and carries whatever was standing there across, at the
new spacing.

**Both have a look of their own**, from the same optional resource pack the pickaxe uses — the art
shipped inert in 0.6.0 and now has items to attach to.

Still one jar for Minecraft 26.1 through the 26.3 line, and still nothing for other players to
install.

releases.notes:
The **Legendary Pickaxe** stops looking like an ordinary netherite pickaxe: a gem of molten amber
set into the head, bleeding warm into the metal around it.

**It arrives as a resource pack, and you can say no.** The server offers it when you join, the way
any server offers a pack. Decline it — or turn server packs off entirely — and you get the vanilla
pickaxe and nothing else changes. No other player has to install anything, and an unmodded client
handles the offer like any other.

**Ordinary pickaxes keep their look.** The pack does not replace the netherite pickaxe's texture; it
adds a second appearance that only the legendary selects, and every other pickaxe in the world falls
through to the vanilla one. A client without the pack has nothing to fall through *from*, which is
why declining costs nothing but the look.

**A pickaxe crafted before this update keeps the old appearance.** What an item looks like is fixed
when it is made, and the marker is written by the recipe — so a world whose pickaxe already exists
goes on seeing a netherite one. Nothing rewrites an item you are already holding.

**An admin who already serves a pack keeps serving it.** Set `resource-pack` in `server.properties`
and that answer stands; this only fills a silence.

**Fix: moving the Dragon Egg no longer costs you hearts.** Dragging it from slot to slot — or setting
it in an anvil to rename it — read as having lost it, so the five extra hearts came off and your
health was clamped down to match. Putting it back returned the hearts empty, so every rearrangement
quietly cost real health you could not get back. It now counts as carried wherever you are holding
it, including on the cursor mid-drag.

Still one jar for Minecraft 26.1 through the 26.3 line, and still nothing for other players to
install.

releases.notes:
A fourth legendary: the **Legendary Pickaxe**. Ordinary pickaxes are untouched — this is the first
legendary that shares its item with something you can still make normally.

**Getting it.** One recipe, built around a netherite pickaxe:

|   |   |   |
|---|---|---|
| Netherite ingot | Deepslate emerald ore | Netherite ingot |
| Efficiency V book | Netherite pickaxe | Efficiency V book |
| Deepslate coal ore | Sculk shrieker | Deepslate coal ore |

Every ore in it, and the shrieker, are Silk Touch drops — which is what the pickaxe then carries, so
the tool that makes one could have mined its own ingredients.

**The books are checked when you take the result.** A recipe can ask for an enchanted book and cannot
ask what is written in it, so two books of the wrong enchantment assemble a pickaxe that refuses to
come out and says why.

**Carrying it.** Unbreakable, **Efficiency VI and Silk Touch** — a level past what an enchanting
table will give you — and **Fire Resistance** for as long as it is in your inventory or your hand.

**Gravel.** It digs gravel as fast as a netherite shovel does, so with Efficiency VI on top it is an
Efficiency VI shovel for that one block. Nothing else a shovel is for changes. Silk Touch means
gravel always comes up as gravel, so this is not the tool to dig flint with.

**It keeps the rules the others do** — refused by every container, never left on display, returned to
the pedestal rather than lost, and one per world.

**The pedestal now holds four.** A world that already has one rebuilds its plinth once on the next
load and carries whatever was standing on it across, at the new spacing.

**A grindstone no longer strips a legendary.** It used to take anything enchanted, so the Netherite
Spear could be ground back to a plain spear and its Lunge III, Sharpness V, Fire Aspect II and
Looting III were gone for good — no enchanting table will give you those again. Grindstones and
anvils now make nothing at all out of a legendary; you can still put one in and take it back out.

Still one jar for Minecraft 26.1 through the 26.3 line, still nothing for other players to install.
